label: Delimiter step (<DEL>), stronger for longer sequences containing p/s/f/b
explanation: Mostly a delimiter unit: 85% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t == L), where it fires in about 49% of sequences, and it holds all of the top activations. Whether and how strongly it fires at <DEL> depends on the prefix. It is more likely and larger when the sequence is longer (delimiter-step rate rises with L) and when the original tokens include p, s, f, b (also j, a, z, g); sequences starting with b are enriched. Prefixes made mostly of digits or tokens like c, h, i, x, o tend not to trigger it. Gating the delimiter step on having seen at least two of {p,s,f,b,j,a,z,g} only moves F1 from 0.59 to 0.64 (precision 0.71, recall 0.58), so the token dependence is graded rather than a clean rule. Secondary weak activity, about 13% of mass, comes from late original-phase steps (rate grows with position, t = 4..8) at first occurrences of a token, again mostly in p/s/f/b-rich sequences. A small amount (2%) comes from the first copy step. It is essentially silent at t = 0..1 and in the copy phase after recall_idx 1.
